stem:
An 8-month-old boy who is exclusively breastfed has become floppy over 6 weeks, has stopped reaching for toys and no longer babbles. He had a cold 3 weeks ago. His mother had weight-loss surgery 4 years ago and stopped the injections prescribed afterwards when she became pregnant; she feels well. He is pale, with no jaundice or organomegaly.

| Test | Result | Reference range |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Haemoglobin | 78 g/L | 105–135 |
| MCV | 96 fL | 70–86 |
| Reticulocytes | 12 × 10⁹/L | 25–100 |
| Bilirubin | 14 µmol/L | 3–20 |

Which diagnosis best unifies the neurological and haematological findings?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Transient erythroblastopenia follows a viral illness and causes anaemia with very low reticulocytes, which makes it tempting here. But it is normocytic, usually occurs between 1 and 4 years, and does not cause developmental regression.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Anaemia of inflammation is mild and normocytic or microcytic, with no neurological effects.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Hereditary spherocytosis causes haemolysis, with jaundice, splenomegaly and high reticulocytes.

options.label: D
options.explanation: G6PD deficiency causes episodes of haemolysis after an oxidant trigger, with jaundice and high reticulocytes.

options.label: E
options.explanation: Correct. Macrocytic anaemia with low reticulocytes and loss of motor, language and social skills in an exclusively breastfed infant points to vitamin B12 deficiency. Weight-loss surgery impairs B12 absorption, his mother stopped her B12 injections, and her milk is low in B12 even though she feels well; his stores at birth also depended on her. Both need treatment, and early treatment can reverse much of the regression.

options.label: F
options.explanation: Acute blood loss causes a normocytic anaemia with a rising reticulocyte count.

options.label: G
options.explanation: Autoimmune haemolytic anaemia causes jaundice and high reticulocytes, with a positive direct antiglobulin test.

options.label: H
options.explanation: Beta-thalassaemia major presents in the second half of the first year with severe anaemia, but it is microcytic, with hepatosplenomegaly and no regression.

context: A breastfed infant with macrocytic anaemia and developmental regression has vitamin B12 deficiency until proven otherwise. Look for the maternal cause, such as a vegan diet, pernicious anaemia or weight-loss surgery without B12 replacement, even if the mother is well.
